lede: The exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO is the thread running through today's web. It shows up on the AI news wire, in the Wikipedia cluster, and on Polymarket, where traders put the odds of his return by November 30 at just under 9 percent. The same news pulled U.S. stocks lower as bond yields climbed. Over on Wikipedia the day's most-read article has nothing to do with any of it: Archive of Our Own, the fan fiction library, at 860,729 views.

throughlines.title: Will Jensen Huang rejoin NVIDIA by November 30, 2026?
throughlines.gist: Huang's departure from Nvidia is live across three unrelated feeds at once, the AI news wire, Polymarket, and Wikipedia, which is what makes it the day's center of gravity rather than a single-outlet rumor.

throughlines.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
throughlines.gist: A Lemmy argument that all AI-generated code should be open source, upvoted 625 times, lands the same day Alibaba's open-sourced AI code-review tool trends on GitHub with 52,000 stars, two angles on the same question of who owns machine-written code.

throughlines.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
throughlines.gist: A writeup of a universal cross-site-scripting hole in uBlock Origin's element picker, one a malicious page can trigger, is leading Hacker News with 233 points, a sharp bug because the extension runs on nearly every page its users load.
